issue.title: CI has no retry or distinct reporting for GitHub Actions platform failures in "Set up job"
issue.description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-fq.8.3 (epic sase-fq.8) as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP; independently verified from the run pages by the sase-fq.8 land agent, and NOT caused by that epic.

WHAT HAPPENS: a hosted-runner incident makes a whole master CI run read as red with zero code signal, because jobs fail in GitHub's own 'Set up job' step before any repo step executes. Two consecutive master runs, both verified directly:

- Run 31114984919 (sha 7cbfc3449): published-core-minimum-smoke, perf-floors and coverage-contexts each failed with 'Set up job' as the only failing step. Annotations: 'The job was not acquired by Runner of type hosted even after multiple attempts' (published-core-minimum-smoke), 'Failed to resolve action download info' and 'Service Unavailable' (build-core). build-core, lint and visual-test were green and the three test legs ran the full suite, so the run's actual code signal was fine.
- Run 31116699976 (sha 628708a71): build-core itself died the same way ('Failed to resolve action download info', 'Service Unavailable'), which skipped docs-build, coverage-contexts, test, lint, visual-test and perf-floors -- all reported '- <job> in 0s'. Zero tests ran on that run at all.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is the specific thing that made epic sase-fq hard to land. Its exit criterion was 'every job in the sase CI workflow passes on master', and for two rounds the only way to tell a platform outage from a real regression was to open each failed job and check whether 'Set up job' was the failing step. Any gate, agent, or human reading run conclusion == failure gets a false regression signal, and re-running is currently a manual decision made after that inspection.

CURRENT STATE: .github/workflows/ci.yml has timeout-minutes on every job (line 23 comment explains why) but no retry, no continue-on-error, and nothing that classifies a setup-phase failure differently from a test failure. Nothing in the repo reruns a job.

SCOPE (a decision, then one of two implementations):
1. Retry: make the setup-phase failures retryable -- e.g. a workflow_run-triggered rerun-failed-jobs job that reruns only jobs whose failure is confined to 'Set up job', bounded to one retry, or an action-level retry wrapper. Note build-core is the fan-out root, so retrying it is worth more than retrying any leaf.
2. Classification: leave the run red but make the redness legible -- a job-summary or annotation step that names which failed jobs executed zero repo steps, so 'platform failure' is distinguishable from 'tests failed' without opening each job.

Option 2 is strictly cheaper and already unblocks the reader; option 1 also unblocks automation. Pick deliberately and pin whichever lands with a test in tests/test_github_actions_ci.py, which is already the workflow-shape contract surface and is in tests/contract_manifest.txt.

OUT OF SCOPE: the 3.12-leg sase_core_rs NameError storm (bead sase-fs) and the ACE parallel flakes (bead sase-ct), which are real test failures on the same runs and tracked separately.

payload.entry: THIRD CONSECUTIVE OCCURRENCE, observed live while landing sase-fq.8: master CI run 31118652934 (sha b694c00c1, pushed 16:06Z) lost BOTH published-core-minimum-smoke and build-core to 'The job was not acquired by Runner of type hosted even after multiple attempts' after 15m2s each, which skipped docs-build, visual-test, coverage-contexts, perf-floors, test and lint ('- <job> in 0s'). Three master runs in a row (31114984919, 31116699976, 31118652934) now have zero or partial code signal for platform reasons, and the third one blocked this epic from getting a second independent CI confirmation of its own fix at HEAD. That is the concrete cost this bead is about.

evidence.note:
FOURTH AND FIFTH CONSECUTIVE OCCURRENCE, blocking a second epic's landing (sase-gg.land, 2026-08-06 ~18:50Z). Independently verified from the run pages.

- Master CI run 31123018619 (sha baebfcd21): visual-test and test (3.13) both failed with 'The job was not acquired by Runner of type hosted even after multiple attempts' as the only annotation. Every job that DID acquire a runner was green — build-core, published-core-minimum-smoke, perf-floors, lint, coverage-contexts, test (3.12), test (3.14). So the run's code signal was fully green and the run still reads red.
- Master CI run 31125302652 (sha 8fcc2520f, pushed 18:10Z): still queued 47 minutes later with only build-core and published-core-minimum-smoke started. Its sibling workflows on the same sha already died the same way — Publish run 31125302861 ('release' job) and Deploy Docs run 31125302614, both 'The job was not acquired by Runner of type hosted'.

WHAT THIS ADDS: (1) The failure mode has widened beyond the CI workflow — the Publish and Deploy Docs workflows are hitting the identical runner-acquisition failure, so a classification/retry fix scoped only to .github/workflows/ci.yml would leave two workflows still emitting false red. (2) It is not confined to this repo: sase-org/sase-core PR #89's CI run 31120460060 lost BOTH jobs to the same annotation, and a manual rerun sat queued for 6+ minutes. (3) Concrete landing cost, second epic running: epic sase-gg's exit criterion is 'confirm a full CI run is green'. Its verify phase (sase-gg.5) was left holding on a CI monitor and closed without ever recording verification evidence; the land agent had to substitute local runs plus per-job annotation inspection to distinguish platform failure from regression. That is exactly the manual inspection this bead proposes to remove, and it has now cost two consecutive epics.

payload.entry: Backlog triage 2026-08-06 (master 25285417d), closed as one group. sase-ge — the three consecutive master runs that failed in GitHub's own 'Set up job' step (31114984919, 31116699976, 31118652934) are real and did cost epic sase-fq a landing round trip, but the cause is a hosted-runner incident, not repo state; the remediation is either a retry wrapper or a legibility annotation for a transient upstream problem. Refile if setup-phase failures keep costing landings once the current incident window has passed, since the cheap half (option 2, classify rather than retry) stays valid. sase-g8 — a sase-core fixture flake ('fatal: could not parse HEAD') observed exactly once in run 31099595038 that passed on a re-run of the same tree; one occurrence is not enough signal to chase a race, so refile with a second occurrence. sase-gh — explicitly ordered after sase-org/sase-core PR #89 merges, and that PR is still OPEN as of 2026-08-06 (verified via gh pr view); the check it adds fails by design against the current package init, so it cannot land yet. Refile once PR #89 merges.

payload.close_reason: Backlog triage 2026-08-06: cause or remediation sits outside this repo's control right now (GitHub platform incident, a once-seen sase-core flake, and work blocked on sase-core PR #89). Cut to bring the ready task queue from 30 to 7.
